local_facts.claim: Caltrans describes the approximately eight-mile US 101 corridor from south of Salinas to Chualar as a daily route for residents, commuters, farmworkers, freight operators, and regional agricultural transport. The corridor has 11 at-grade intersections and seven at-grade rail crossings.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A collision near Salinas can involve more than two privately owned cars. A crew vehicle, work pickup, produce truck, or other farm-related vehicle may require early attention to ownership, work use, vehicle markings, dispatch records, and the exact intersection or access point. Those facts do not establish fault, but they identify evidence that may not be obvious at the scene.
local_facts.title: Agricultural traffic changes the evidence search

local_facts.claim: California's Office of Traffic Safety recorded 503 people killed or injured in Salinas traffic crashes in 2023. Its Salinas ranking lists 57 hit-and-run and 63 speed-related fatal-and-injury collisions that year.
local_facts.why_it_matters: These figures do not decide an individual claim. They show why the specific report, scene location, vehicle evidence, witness information, treatment records, and insurance documents must be preserved instead of relying on a general account of how crashes happen in the city.
local_facts.title: City-wide crash data is context, not proof

local_facts.claim: Monterey County Superior Court's local rules place civil proceedings in the Monterey Division, with the civil division at the Monterey Courthouse. The rules allow non-mandatory electronic filings to be delivered at Salinas, Marina, or Monterey and provide that a filing received at an authorized courthouse is date-stamped when received before routing to the location with appropriate jurisdiction.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A Salinas crash does not mean every civil step takes place at the Salinas Courthouse. If a claim advances beyond insurance, the pleadings, venue, court rules, and timing need to be handled through the county's actual civil-division structure rather than assumed from the collision location.
local_facts.title: Civil cases follow Monterey County's division rules

anchors.label: Percentage ceiling on an injury fee
anchors.detail: Rule 1.5 of the California Rules of Professional Conduct bars an unconscionable or illegal fee and then lists thirteen factors for testing one. It prints no percentage for ordinary negligence work.
anchors.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5(a)-(b)

anchors.label: First paper in an unlimited civil case, Monterey County
anchors.detail: Charged by the Monterey County Superior Court on the complaint in any case pleading more than $35,000, and again on the first paper filed by each other party.
anchors.source_name: Monterey County Superior Court civil fee schedule

anchors.label: Advance jury fee, nonrefundable
anchors.detail: One side of the case posts it or the right to a jury is waived. Daily juror deposits after the first day are set by the court on top of it.

anchors.label: Health plan lien ceiling once a lawyer is involved
anchors.detail: A managed-care or medical-group reimbursement lien cannot take more than a third of the money due to the injured person under a judgment, compromise or settlement.

fee_rows.stage: The fee itself, in a crash claim
fee_rows.note: Tested after the fact against thirteen listed factors, among them proportionality to the work, the results obtained, and whether the client gave informed consent.
fee_rows.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5(b)

fee_rows.note: Malpractice-specific statute. Twenty-five percent where the claim settles before a complaint or arbitration demand is filed, thirty-three percent after, and more only by motion on good cause.

fee_rows.share: Duplicate signed copy, four required statements
fee_rows.note: It must state the rate, how costs affect both the fee and the recovery, any charges for related matters, and that the fee is not set by law but is negotiable.
The $35,000 pleading line decides which tier applies, and the limited tier splits again at $10,000.
fee_rows.source_name: Monterey County Superior Court civil fee schedule

fee_rows.stage: Motions and a summary judgment motion
fee_rows.note: Each paper requiring a hearing draws sixty dollars; a summary judgment or summary adjudication motion draws five hundred.
fee_rows.source_name: Monterey County Superior Court civil fee schedule

fee_rows.stage: Costs recoverable if the case is won
fee_rows.note: Filing, motion and jury fees, depositions, service of process and court-ordered expert fees are on it. Investigation expenses and experts the court did not order are not.
